resolved.value: A THIRTEEN-YEAR-OLD's body, and it is not an adult woman's: small and short with a child's proportions — no length in the limbs yet, a flat straight torso, narrow hips barely wider than the waist, and no adult curves. Strong for her size, with real definition in the shoulders, upper back and thighs from the sport. Lean, dense and compact. Reproduce this body as it is: do NOT lengthen her, do NOT give her an adult figure, do NOT slim or thicken her.

resolved.value: A POWDER BLUE LONG-SLEEVED gymnastics LEOTARD exactly as photo2.png shows it: a V-neck edged in ROYAL BLUE; across the chest a CHEVRON pointing DOWN to a point at the sternum, made of TWO parallel bands, and their order is not open to interpretation: the band that touches the powder blue CHEST above it is WHITE, and the band that touches the powder blue BELLY below it is ROYAL BLUE — white on the shoulder side, royal blue on the stomach side; the same white-then-royal-blue chevron repeated at each CUFF, so each wrist ends in a royal blue band. The body of the leotard is plain powder blue, high-cut at the legs. The number 0 sits on the OUTSIDE of her LEFT UPPER SLEEVE near the shoulder, drawn as a WHITE OUTLINE with the powder blue showing inside it. A small WHITE SCRIPT MAKER'S MARK sits low on her LEFT HIP — her own kit's mark, small and soft-edged, never enlarged and never redrawn. No club name, no player name, no sponsor. The BACK of the leotard is not visible in any photograph; the DECISION is that it stays PLAIN: the same chevron carries round across the upper back, and below it the back is smooth powder blue with NO number, NO name and NO lettering. This kit carries its number on the LEFT SLEEVE, and a second one across the shoulders would print a mark this leotard does not have.
resolved.why: read off zoomed crops of photo2.png by hand (2026-08-22). The resolver saw the chevron and the cuffs but not the sleeve number, the royal blue neckline edge or the hip mark. Back recorded as a decision 2026-08-22 after the kit plate invented a large 0 across it — third sport in a row to try it (README §36). Band ORDER restated 2026-08-22 in terms of what each band touches: 'a white band with a royal blue band below it' produced the inverse twice, once as a fresh plate and once as an edit. On a V-shaped chevron 'above/below' is ambiguous — 'the band touching the chest' is not.
